questions.stem:
Identify the CORRECT set of details from the following :
A. $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ : Inner orbital complex; $d^{2}sp^{3}$ hybridized
B. $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$ : Outer orbital complex; $sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridized
C. $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ : Outer orbital complex; $d^{2}sp^{3}$ hybridized
D. $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$ : Outer orbital complex; $sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridized
E. $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ : Inner orbital complex; $sp^{3}$ hybridized
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
(A) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ : $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ : $d^{6}$
$\mathrm{NH_3}$ : Strong $\rightarrow$ forced pairing
So, complex is inner orbital complex and $d^{2}sp^{3}$.
(B) $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$ : $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ : $d^{4}$ : $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ : weak
So, complex is outer orbital complex and $sp^{3}d^{2}$
(C) $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ : $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ : $d^{6}$ : $\mathrm{F^-}$ : weak
complex is outer orbtal complex and $sp^{3}d^{2}$.
(D) $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$ : $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ : $d^{5}$ : $\mathrm{F^-}$ : weak,
complex is outer orbital complex and $sp^{3}d^{2}$
(E) $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2}}$ : $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ : $d^{8}$ : $\mathrm{\bar{C}N}$ : strong, forced pairing $\rightarrow$ square planar
So, inner orbital complex and $dsp^{2}$

questions.stem: Consider the above electrochemical cell where a metal electrode (M) is undergoing redox reaction by forming $\mathrm{M^+}$ ($\mathrm{M \rightarrow M^+ + e^-}$). The cation $\mathrm{M^+}$ is present in two different concentrations $c_1$ and $c_2$ as shown above. Which of the following statement is correct for generating a positive cell potential ?
questions.solution:
When $C_1$ is anode :
Anode : $\mathrm{M \rightarrow M^+ + e^-}$ ($C_1$)
Cathode : $\mathrm{M^+ + e^- \rightarrow M}$ ($C_2$)
------------------------------
$\mathrm{M^+ + e^- \rightarrow M}$ (with $c_2$ under $\mathrm{M^+}$ and $c_1$ under M)
So, $E_{cell} = -\frac{RT}{nF}\ln\frac{C_1}{C_2} = \frac{RT}{nF}\ln\frac{C_2}{C_1}$
for, positive cell potential $C_2 > C_1$
When $C_1$ is cathode, then cell reaction
$\mathrm{M^+ + e^- \rightarrow M}$ (with $C_1$ under $\mathrm{M^+}$ and $C_2$ under M)
So, $E_{cell} = -\frac{RT}{nF}\ln\frac{C_1}{C_2}$
Hence, $C_1 > C_2$ for positive cell potential.

options.text: If $c_1$ is present at anode, then $c_1 > c_2$.
If $c_1$ is present at anode, then $c_1 = c_2$.
If $c_1$ is present at cathode, then $c_1 > c_2$.
If $c_1$ is present at cathode, then $c_1 < c_2$.

Identify the INCORRECT statements from the following :
A. Notation $\mathrm{^{24}_{12}Mg}$ represents 24 protons and 12 neutrons.
B. Wavelength of a radiation of frequency $4.5 \times 10^{15}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$ is $6.7 \times 10^{-8}$ m.
C. One radiation has wavelength = $\lambda_1$ (900 nm) and energy = $E_1$. Other radiation has wavelength = $\lambda_2$ (300 nm) and energy = $E_2$. $E_1 : E_2 = 3 : 1$.
D. Number of photons of light of wavelength 2000 pm that provides 1 J of energy is $1.006 \times 10^{16}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
A. $\mathrm{^{24}_{12}Mg}$ represents 24 mass number and 12 protons
B. Frequency, $V = 4.5 \times 10^{15}\ \mathrm{s^{-2}}$; $\lambda = \frac{c}{y} = \frac{3 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{ms^{-2}}}{4.5 \times 10^{15}} = 6.7 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{m}$
C. $\lambda_1 = 900\ \mathrm{nm}$; Energy = $E_1$ and $\lambda_2 = 300\ \mathrm{nm}$, Energy = $E_2$
as $E \propto \frac{1}{\lambda}$; $\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} = \frac{E_2}{E_1} \Rightarrow \frac{900}{300} \Rightarrow \frac{E_2}{E_1} \Rightarrow \frac{E_1}{E_2} = \frac{1}{3}$
D. $\lambda = 2000\ \mathrm{pm} = 2000 \times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{m}$ ; $E = 1\ \mathrm{J}$.
as $E = \frac{nhc}{\lambda}$; $n = \frac{E\lambda}{hc} = \frac{1 \times 2000 \times 10^{-12}}{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^{8}}$
$= 100.614 \times 10^{14} = 1.006 \times 10^{16}$

questions.stem:
Observe the following reactions at T(K).
I. $\mathrm{A \rightarrow products}$
II. $\mathrm{5Br^-(aq) + BrO_3^-(aq) + 6H^+(aq) \rightarrow 3Br_2(aq) + 3H_2O}(l)$
Both the reactions are started at 10.00 am. The rates of these reactions at 10.10 am are same. The value of $-\frac{\Delta[\mathrm{Br^-}]}{\Delta t}$ at 10.10 am is $2 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}\,min^{-1}}$. The concentration of A at 10.10 am is $10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$.
What is the first order rate constant (in $\mathrm{min^{-1}}$) of reaction I ?
questions.solution:
At 10 : 10am $\frac{-\Delta[\mathrm{Br^-}]}{\Delta t} = 2 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}\,min^{-1}}$
$$\text{Rate} = \frac{-1}{5}\frac{\Delta[\mathrm{Br^-}]}{\Delta t} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-4}}{5}\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}\,min^{-1}}$$
At 10 : 10am, rate of both reactions is same, so : for reaction I : Rate = k[A]
$$\frac{2 \times 10^{-4}}{5} = k \times 10^{-2}$$
$$k = \frac{2 \times 10^{-2}}{5} = 4 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{min^{-1}}$$

questions.stem:
200 cc of $x \times 10^{-3}$ M potassium dichromate is required to oxidise 750 cc of 0.6 M Mohr's salt solution in acidic medium.
Here x = _______ .
questions.solution:
Mohr's salt : $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4FeSO_4{,}6H_2O}$
Volume = 750 ml, molarity = 0.6 M
moles of Mohr's salt = $750 \times 0.6$ m moles = moles of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$
Reaction involed :
$$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ + 6Fe^{2+} \rightarrow 6Fe^{3+} + 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O}$$
from reaction,
6 moles of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ react with = 1 mole of $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$
So, $750 \times 0.6$ m moles of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ will react with
$= \frac{1}{6} \times 750 \times 0.6 = 75$ m moles of $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$
Moles of $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ = 75 m moles = volume $\times$ molarity
$$\text{molarity} = \frac{75\ \text{mmoles}}{200\ \text{ml}} = \frac{75}{200}\ \mathrm{mol/L} = 0.375\ \mathrm{mol/L}$$
$x \times 10^{-3} = 0.375$
$x = 375$

questions.stem: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At 320 K, the vapour pressure for the solution, containing 3 mol of A and 1 mol of B is 500 mm Hg. At the same temperature, if 1 mol of A is further added to this solution, vapour pressure of the solution increases by 20 mm Hg. Vapour pressure (in mm Hg) of B in pure state is ______ . (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
At 320 K,
Initially, moles of A, $n_A = 3$ moles
moles of B, $n_B = 1$ moles
mole fraction : $x_A = \frac{3}{4}$, $x_B = \frac{1}{4}$
Total pressure, 500 mm of Hg = $x_A P_A^0 + x_B P_B^0$
$\frac{3P_A^0}{4} + \frac{P_B^0}{4} = 500$ mm of Hg
$3P_A^0 + P_B^0 = 2000$ mm of Hg ...(1)
On adding 1 mole of a : $n'_A = 4$; $n'_B = 1$
$x'_A = \frac{4}{5}$; $x'_B = \frac{1}{5}$
Total pressure, $520 = \frac{4}{5}P_A^0 + \frac{P_B^0}{5}$
$4P_A^0 + P_B^0 = 2600$ mm of Hg ...(2)
Subtracting (1) from (2), we get
$P_A^0 = 600$ mm of Hg
as $3P_A^0 + P_B^0 = 2000$
So, $1800 + P_B^0 = 2000$
$P_B^0 = 200$ mm of Hg

In compound (Q), the percentage of oxygen is ________ %. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
[Scheme shown in solution figure: benzene + $\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_2-CO-Cl}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{anhydrous } \mathrm{AlCl_3}}$ P = $\mathrm{C_6H_5-CO-CH_2-CH_2-CO-CH_3}$; with aq. NaOH the carbanion $\mathrm{-CO-\bar{C}H_2}$ attacks the benzoyl C=O intramolecularly giving 3-hydroxy-3-phenylcyclopentanone, which on heating ($\Delta$) loses water to give Q = 3-phenylcyclopent-2-en-1-one]

questions.stem:
$$\mathrm{X_2(g) + Y_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2Z(g)}$$
$\mathrm{X_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{Y_2(g)}$ are adeed to a 1 L flask and it is found that the system attains the above equilibrium at T(K) with the number of moles of $\mathrm{X_2(g)}$, $\mathrm{Y_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{Z(g)}$ being 3, 3 and 9 mol respectively (equilibrium moles). Under this condition of equilibrium, 10 mol of $\mathrm{Z(g)}$ is added to the flask and the temperature is maintained at T(K). Then the number of moles of $\mathrm{Z(g)}$ in the flask when the new equilibrium is established is ______. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{X_2(g) + Y_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2Z(g)}$ Volume = 1L
at equilibium concentration : 3M | 3M | 9M
$$K_C = \frac{[Z]^2}{[X_2][Y_2]} = \frac{9^2}{3 \times 3} = 9$$
New concentration when 10 mol Z is added
$\mathrm{X_2(g) + Y_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2Z(g)}$
3M | 3M | 19M
$Q_C = \frac{(19)^2}{3 \times 3} = 40.11 > K_C$. So, reaction moves backward
At new equilibirum
$\mathrm{X_2(g) + Y_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2Z(g)}$
at equilibrium : $3 + a$ | $3 + a$ | $19 - 2a$
$$K_C = 9 = \frac{(19 - 2a)^2}{(3 + a)(3 + a)}$$
$$\left(\frac{19 - 2a}{3 + a}\right)^2 = 9$$
$\frac{19 - 2a}{3 + a} = 3 \Rightarrow 19 - 2a = 9 + 3a$
$5a = 10$
$a = 2$
New concentration of Z(g) = $19 - 2a = 19 - 4 = 15$ mol/L
moles = $15\ \mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}} \times 1\ \mathrm{L} = 15$ moles
